judgements.justification: B's chair raised a 7, 7, 7, 6 paper to a spotlight that no reviewer asked for, adding its own 'strong and elegant' praise.
Neither committee's recommendation rests on a forecast of impact beyond cortical surface reconstruction.
Only A's oT7u moved, from 4 to 5, and it still asked for rejection; the rebuttal changed neither recommendation.
B's wgwm (bulleted, 2.5 h, no reply, wrong claims) and 4s5o (confidence 2, minor comments) gave 7s on little scrutiny.
A's decisive concerns (unclear Section 3.1, missing loss and proof, no grid-based baseline) were shared with B; A-only points such as EMD and crossing surfaces were not its stated grounds.
Both saw the unclear Section 3.1, missing loss and proof, and unclear novelty; A made them decisive, B treated them as camera-ready fixes and weighted the speed-up.
No score moved because of reviewer discussion in either committee.
A's iY4e praised the experiments and named mostly addressable points, yet gave a 4 that its text does not explain.
No A reviewer said it could not judge the paper; A's reviewers gave clear reject verdicts, not hedged borderline scores.
A's chair restated oT7u's argument, but oT7u's 5 was not an outlier in A's 4, 3, 5, 5.
The committees' verbal verdicts differed (major revision versus accept), so the split is not a scale-calibration gap.
B had no dissent and no score above 7, but A's scores were lower, not a spread at a similar or higher mean, and B's chair did not cite agreement as grounds.
No score rose to cause the split; oT7u's rise to 5 on clarifications left A at reject and moved it toward B.
B's meta-review called prior work 'the only controversy' and omitted EX4h's point that the accuracy gain over DeepCSR is small, and xE8n's warning on significance.
The wrong claims (wgwm's Lipschitz and limitations, 4s5o's %SIF, iY4e's loss) are not misstatements of the results that fed a score across the split.
The authors told B the method is 'as competitive as DeepCSR' in accuracy and conceded the novelty overstatement, yet no B score fell and the chair gave a spotlight.
No objection came after the response period in either committee.
The scores differ widely (4, 3, 5, 5 versus 7, 7, 7, 6), so the split is not a tier cut-off on near-identical reviews.
B's best-informed reviewer xE8n warned 'I would not overstate the significance' and doubted the fit; the chair reused xE8n's praise but gave a spotlight on the scores.
A's concerns were fixable clarifications, but A still judged the fix too large; B's novelty concern did not hold B's scores down.
Neither committee had an outlying score.
No outlying reviewer exists in either committee.
B had no discarded detractor; A did not weigh a higher tier.
Only B's xE8n doubted the NeurIPS fit, and B ended higher, so venue fit did not lower one committee.
Neither meta-review misreported reviewers' final positions or what the response answered; B's omission is covered by R14.
Three B reviewers did not reply, but the response did not answer points that would have changed their already high scores; the split does not come from unrevised scores.
B's 4s5o (confidence 2, 'Math/other details were not carefully checked') gave a 7 that B's chair counted in full, leaning on the scores.
Neither committee split evenly between accept and reject.
The authors' answers to the two committees do not conflict in substance.
B's wgwm called the paper 'well embedded into the existing literature' and accepted the 'new diffeomorphic mesh transform' claim that the decade of mesh LDDMM work contradicts.
B's spotlight exceeds 7, 7, 7, 6 with no reviewer asking for it, and the meta-review gives no reason for that tier.
A's critics objected to exposition and baselines, not to the paper's framing from a neighbouring field's premises.
No reviewer in either committee rated above 7 or argued for the paper against its critics.

added.name: Promised fixes judged too large without re-review
added.definition: One committee's reviewers or area chair accepted that the authors' promised revisions addressed the paper's faults but rejected it because those revisions were too large to accept without another round of review, while the other committee treated the same fixes as camera-ready changes.
added.justification: R06 covers different weight on a flaw, but here A's decisive step was a policy on conditional acceptance: it took the rebuttal's fixes as adequate yet refused to accept them unseen. R13 is the opposite case, where promised revisions raised scores.

reasoning: Both committees saw the same faults: an unclear Section 3.1, a missing loss and proof, unclear novelty over diffeomorphic registration, and no grid-based baseline. A judged these a major revision needing a new review round; B treated them as camera-ready fixes and weighted the 500-fold speed-up (R06, new R34). B's high scores rest partly on thin or low-confidence reviews (R04, R27) and on an accepted novelty claim that its own expert refuted (R30). B's chair then gave a spotlight with no reviewer support or stated grounds, past the expert's warning and the authors' accuracy concession, and omitted the weaknesses from its meta-review (R01, R14, R16, R19, R31). A's iY4e gave a 4 that its text does not explain (R08).
